name: How rockets get to space

hook_variants.template: Getting to space isn't about going up. It's about going sideways.
{news_title} Here's the physics behind every launch.
Twenty-eight thousand kilometers an hour. That's what 'orbiting' means.

sections.text: Rocket science is simpler than it sounds. Throw mass backward, go forward.
The station circles 400 kilometers up, at 28,000 kilometers an hour.

sections.text: Orbiting is a speed problem. Go sideways fast enough and you keep falling around Earth.
